sanskrit: तेजः क्षमा धृतिः शौचमद्रोहो नातिमानिता । भवन्ति सम्पदं दैवीमभिजातस्य भारत ॥
hindiTranslation: तेज प्रभाव, क्षमा, धैर्य, शरीरकी शुद्धि, वैरभावका न रहना और मानको न चाहना, हे भरतवंशी अर्जुन  ये सभी दैवी सम्पदाको प्राप्त हुए मनुष्यके लक्षण हैं ॥
englishTranslation: Splendor, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, absence of hostility, and lack of pride belong to the one born with divine qualities, O Bharata.
essence: True strength looks like forgiveness, steadiness, and no need to dominate.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: A person with noble qualities shows strength, forgiveness, steadiness, purity, no hostility, and no pride.
simpleInsight: You can measure character by how powerfully someone stays gentle.
detailedMeaning: Krishna lists the qualities that mark a noble person. After naming nonviolence, truth, and self-control, he adds the traits that make divine character visible in action.
modernRelevance: A brother who was cheated in a land deal still attends his cousin's wedding without bitterness. Krishna lists forgiveness, steadiness and absence of hostility as marks of a divine nature, visible in moments like that.
translationLiteral: तेजः (splendor) / क्षमा (forgiveness) / धृतिः (steadiness) / शौचम् (purity) / अद्रोहः (absence of hostility) / नातिमानिता (lack of pride) / भवन्ति (become) / सम्पदम् (attainment) / दैवीम् (divine) / अभिजातस्य (of one born) / भारत (O Bharata)
insight: Forgiveness, steadiness, purity and freedom from pride complete Krishna's portrait of the person born with divine qualities.

quoteVariants.text: Divine character shows itself as strength, forgiveness, and humility.
Strength without pride. Forgiveness without weakness.
Real strength leaves no room for pride.
